speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Members will agree that Singapore’s politics must be for Singaporeans alone to decide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Worryingly, however, the Internet and social media have created a new, vast and easy playing field for foreign interference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Among others, we have read about foreign interference in the politics of the United States (US), United Kingdom (UK), Ukraine, Australia, France, Germany, the Netherlands and New Zealand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Clandestine and sophisticated tactics were used to fracture social cohesion and influence election outcomes through the spread of disinformation and half-truths and exploitation of sensitive issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In the US, indictments by Special Counsel Robert Mueller lay out how a foreign hostile information campaign systematically and surreptitiously sought to influence the outcome of the 2016 Presidential Elections.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: More than two years before election day, a foreign organisation had started infiltrating American society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: They used fake social media accounts pretending to be real Americans, and created social media groups on controversial issues likely to engage Americans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: These accounts and groups gained influence over time, attracting thousands of real American followers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Social media posts by such fake foreign accounts even found their way into American mainstream media.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The foreign actor was sophisticated in its approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It had researched the fault lines in American society and politics, and drove wedges along these lines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Its social media accounts spread falsehoods and false narratives on divisive sociopolitical issues, such as race, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender (LGBT) rights, gun control and immigration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The foreign actor used bots and digital advertisements to amplify its reach and viewpoints rapidly to give the impression that they were popular.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This built a false sense of reality: Americans felt that their views and concerns were echoed by others, without realising that much of the support was artificially generated by fake accounts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Researchers later found evidence that the foreign actor had targeted hotly contested states, such as Wisconsin, Virginia and Pennsylvania, through Facebook advertising campaigns on divisive issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For example, voters in Wisconsin saw more paid ads on guns and race issues, because these issues held more sway with them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Those with household incomes of less than US$40,000 saw more paid ads on the issues of immigration and race.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The campaigns riled up anger and fear, and deepened divisions in the society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Americans were also deceived to believe that they were part of spontaneous local movements when they were, in fact, being manipulated by a foreign actor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In one instance, the foreign organisation cultivated two ideologically opposed fake Facebook accounts, the “United Muslims of America” and the “Heart of Texas”, and organised a protest and counter-protest at the same place and time to orchestrate discord on the streets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Real Americans in both camps turned up and demonstrated in opposition to each other.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This hostile information campaign was not only to influence the outcome of the 2016 Presidential elections.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Its longer-term objective was to undermine America’s institutions and democracy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The campaign polarised and generated deep suspicion within American society and against its institutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We saw a similar pattern of interference in the UK referendum on Brexit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Falsehoods on social media, bots and fake accounts were similarly key tools of foreign interference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Grievances over immigration and a growing sense of disenfranchisement were exploited to turn the British people against UK and European Union (EU) institutions and policies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The 2017 French Presidential Election was also the subject of foreign interference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In the Netherlands, a hostile information campaign sought to undermine support for an EU-Ukraine trade agreement in 2016.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The same year in Germany, a hostile information campaign built upon a fabricated story about a German girl being raped by Arab migrants stirred up anti-immigrant sentiments, sparked demonstrations and eroded public confidence in the German government’s immigration and asylum policy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: At the hearings of the Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods, Ukrainian experts shared their country’s experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Disinformation about the Ukrainian government was spread through foreign media channels and social networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It created the impetus for armed conflict and weakened the resolve of Ukrainians to fight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It eroded trust among Ukrainians in their public institutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The experts highlighted their country’s experience as a cautionary tale, a threat that countries ignore at their peril.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Mr Ruslan Deynychenko, co-Founder of StopFake.org, an Ukranian organisation that counters disinformation, said, “You cannot ignore the existence of propaganda, because Ukraine did it for years, and it might happen with any country that one day you can wake up and look in the window and see people with machine guns who kill each other because somebody on TV persuaded them they should hate each other.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Our experience, again, demonstrated that disinformation is a powerful weapon and it could be pointed to any country at any time very, very quickly.”  He added, “Unfortunately, ignorance of this threat of foreign disinformation cost our country too much.”  We are also seeing other insidious forms of interference, by foreign actors attempting to influence those involved in domestic political discourse through funding and donations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In one instance, a senator resigned after it was revealed that he had received donations from a foreign political donor and advocated that foreign state’s position on a sensitive issue, contradicting his own party’s official position.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: An opposition leader allegedly circumvented political donation laws by disguising a donation made by a businessman linked to a foreign government, so that it did not have to be declared.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It has sparked debate within the country on the need to review policies against foreign interference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Indeed, today, information can easily be weaponised by foreign actors, at low cost, and with anonymity and impunity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This is asymmetric information warfare, fought in a theatre and era with no distinction between war and peace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In this battlefield, Singapore, an open, democratic, digitally-connected and diverse country, is especially vulnerable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We are a young country with sensitive fault lines that foreign actors can exploit to foment distrust and ill-will among our various communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: They can easily deploy the same tactics, both clandestine and overt, that we have seen elsewhere, to undermine our democratic processes and institutions, and subvert our politics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Many of the countries I had mentioned have learnt hard lessons and are taking action to expose and counter foreign interference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We are likewise developing a strategy on two fronts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: First, we need to sensitise Singaporeans to the threat, and nurture a discerning public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We are our own first line of defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We must learn to be sceptical of and be able to discern falsehoods or half-truths and detect foreign actors and their attempts to interfere in our politics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: When they seek to create schisms in our society, we must stand together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We must also take further measures to minimise the possibility of politically-involved individuals and organisations being subverted by foreign actors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We must be able to act swiftly and effectively to disrupt and counter false, misleading and inauthentic information and narratives spread by foreign actors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We must also be able to pre-emptively expose clandestine foreign interference campaigns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In the physical world, foreign actors may interfere in our domestic politics through the use of proxies, by funding or donating to politically-involved individuals and organisations, or by taking on key leadership roles in the organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Our laws must minimise the possibility of such entities being thus used and manipulated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We must not allow foreign actors to undermine our political sovereignty, nor our ability to make our own choices on how we want to govern our country and live our lives.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The first is, have there been instances of foreign interference in Singapore?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Earlier, the Senior Minister of State mentioned that Australia implemented some laws in June 2018.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: What are the gaps in our existing laws and whether new laws will be introduced to address foreign interference?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the 1970s, the Government took two newspapers to task – The Singapore Herald and The Eastern Sun – for taking foreign money and then attempting to undermine the Government.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There have been and will always continue to be countries with an interest in interfering in Singapore's affairs and swaying public opinion amongst us and against us.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: He was expelled in August 2017 and had his Permanent Residency annulled.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: He had knowingly interacted and cooperated with intelligence organisations and agents of a foreign country to influence Singapore's foreign policy and public opinion.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: He had done so by engaging prominent and influential Singaporeans, and giving them what he claimed was privileged information about the foreign country so as to influence their opinions in favour of that said country.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Huang also recruited others in aid of his operations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Minister for Communications and Information had stated that this was the work of an advanced persistent threat group, cyberattackers who are typically state-linked.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are not casual hackers or criminal gangs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Cyber hackings are often deployed in concert with hostile information campaigns to search for information that can be weaponised.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Testimony before the Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods also showed indication of information warfare being carried out against Singapore, including the use of news articles and social media, to influence the minds of segments of the Singapore population.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Foreign interference is not always easy to detect or attribute.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In December last year, when bilateral issues with our immediate neighbour were at the top of the news, we noticed that a curious spike in online comments on social media made from avatar accounts – essentially, anonymous accounts with profile pictures that do not show the owner's face.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Many of these comments were critical of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On one such issue, jams at land checkpoints.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We do not know who these suspicious accounts belong to nor do we know if they are being coordinated by foreign actors.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But it is clear that these accounts had sought to give and create an artificial impression to netizens of the opposition to Singapore's position, at a time of heightened bilateral difficulties.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is not the only issue or instance.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In such instances, it is imperative that we have the ability to identify where these accounts come from and, indeed, if they are real.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In our daily operations, our security agencies take it as a working assumption that we must be careful of the threat of foreign interference.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The overseas examples that I have alluded to attest to this threat.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But it is not convenient, for national security reasons, for me to enumerate all of these examples.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Suffice to say that these threats are real, we are a target, and we must be vigilant.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And on that score and Miss Cheng's second question, the Select Committee had recommended that the Government consider measures to address both deliberate online falsehoods and also state-sponsored campaigns that threaten our national security.
